challenge.better_approach: Filing the red in the house commons was the other option; 58e242c8be4f ruled a worktree's reds out of another checkout's commons, so a trouble is the one loud record left. Raising inside red_tickets would spread the change into the store rule; the device's except branch is the one place that already knows the red went unticketed.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a trouble is the right record rather than a ticket: a trouble is an error needing a human fixer, and an unticketable red needs exactly that (someone re-runs it from a checkout with a commons). That the tester's raiser lands under the scratch HOME in the proof, which the harness pins.
challenge.prior_art: 207c4074b3d5 (each run tickets its new red; its FIXME 1 chose print-and-go-on), 58e242c8be4f (reds cast only into the checkout's own commons), 19193ff1e41e (the commons beside the worktree for hollow runs), 9f5bb43e8a64 and 31b76dfeb864 (ticket commit inside the hook; a red in a ladder goes on). None raises a record for the unticketable case.
challenge.real_collision: 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 said the run goes on: it still does; this adds a record, it does not stop the run. No collision.

answers.falsifier: (1) a red measured in a scratch checkout whose sibling has no CairnCommons raises trouble 'tester-red-unticketed:<proof>' whose why names the proof and the unreachable store, and the run still returns its red record; (2) in that run no file is written under any CairnCommons, the house commons included, and the stderr line 'was NOT ticketed' still prints; (3) the same proof run green afterwards clears that trouble, and a green with no standing trouble writes no clear
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the failure 207c4074b3d5's FIXME 1 left quiet, measured on cairn/devices/tester/device.py
answers.how: In cairn/devices/tester/device.py, the except StoreUnreachable branch keeps its print and emit and adds self.raise_trouble('tester-red-unticketed:' + <proof path relative to the repo, else as given>, why=<names the proof, the store and the reason>, detail={'proof', 'store_reason'}). A raise that itself fails prints and does not kill the run. When a later run of the same proof tickets its red (ticket_what_is_new returns) or the proof runs green, the trouble clears if it stands (read through cairn.devices.trouble.tools.store.store.live, as reseal.run_or_record does). The house commons is never written (58e242c8be4f's wrong_intent). The red-first proof copies cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_red_casts_only_into_its_own_commons.py's harness: a scratch git checkout under a scratch HOME with no CairnCommons beside it, red_tickets.ROOTS pointed at it, and TesterDevice().run_proof on a red fixture inside it (sink='none', isolation='none'), marked testing.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (errors are permanent in records of truth) and 207c4074b3d5 (reds don't get lost, outline 9.4.2.3.7.5)
answers.what: When a tester run measures a red it cannot ticket because the derived ticket store is in no git tree, the red is made permanent in a trouble naming the proof and the store, so it is not lost when the run's stderr scrolls away.

bullets.text: An unticketable red was only a stderr line; it now raises tester-red-unticketed:<proof>.
